conceptZh: 四個方形餐盤環繞一隻攜帶工具的守護小狗，小狗歡快點擊餐盤後，餐盤與小狗順暢演化為「器」字。
object: Four square ceramic snack bowls arranged in a grid around a small helper puppy holding a wooden utensil.
morph: The four square bowls flatten into the four corner '口' components, while the central puppy morphs into the central '犬' component, assembling the character '器'.
creativeAngle: 回歸「器」字本義與字形結構（四口一犬），以「四方形餐具+守護器皿的小狗」作為具象化隱喻，趣味展現器皿與工具概念，兼具文字學幾何特徵與兒童動畫視覺吸引力。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D literacy animation for 6-8 year old Taiwanese children introducing the Traditional Chinese character 器 (qì, meaning vessels and tools).

[00:00 - 02:00] Staging & Intro: On a clean, warm light-beige table, four square turquoise ceramic snack dishes are arranged in a balanced 2x2 grid. In the central space between them stands a playful brown puppy wearing a tiny red apron and holding a small wooden spoon, forming the central figure. The composition is brightly lit with soft warm lighting, keeping the scene uncluttered and perfectly centered.

[00:02 - 04:00] Transformation & Metaphor: The puppy happily barks 'Qi! Qi!' while tapping each dish with its wooden spoon. The four square dishes cleanly flatten into four bold, saturated dark-navy square strokes (口 at top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right). Simultaneously, the puppy stretches gracefully into the central stroke assembly of 犬 (a horizontal stroke, sweeping diagonal legs, and a distinct top-right dot stroke). Every stroke connects precisely according to Traditional Chinese orthography.

[00:04 - 05:00] Final Assembly: The strokes lock together smoothly to form the complete, perfectly balanced Traditional Chinese glyph 器. The character fills 70% of the frame height, centered against the clean background with ample margins.

[00:05 - 08:00] Extended Hold & Audio: The solid dark-navy character 器 holds completely static for 3 full seconds without camera motion, drift, or distracting effects. Over clear background ambience, an authentic Taiwanese Mandarin child voiceover clearly repeats 'ㄑㄧˋ! ㄑㄧˋ! ㄑㄧˋ! 器 (qì) - 器皿的器!' three to four times.

conceptZh: 一隻俏皮的機械玩具機器人興奮開啟四周四個方形工具盒，身體與工具盒順暢演變成「器」字。
object: A colorful mechanical toy robot and four square tool trays
morph: The four tool trays flatten into the four 口 square strokes, while the toy robot's springy frame stretches into the central 犬 strokes to form the character 器.
creativeAngle: 回應家長「機器人」與「生動搞笑」的需求，利用玩具機器人過度興奮引發的彈跳拉伸動作創造喜劇笑點，精準對應「器」字的四口一犬結構。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animation introducing the Traditional Chinese character 器 (qì).

[00:00 - 00:02] Staging & Setup:
On a clean, brightly lit light-cream surface, four square turquoise toy tool trays are arranged in a symmetric 2x2 grid. In the center between the trays stands a chunky, colorful mechanical toy robot with springy joints and round glowing eyes. The composition is uncluttered, brightly lit with soft shadows, keeping the subjects centered.

[00:02 - 00:04.5] Visual Gag & Transformation:
The toy robot enthusiastically presses a red chest button to showcase its gadgets. With a funny springy boing, the four square tool trays pop open and neatly flatten into four bold, dark-indigo square strokes (口 at top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right). Surprised by the sudden pop, the toy robot's mechanical frame hilariously stretches out—its arms extend into a solid horizontal bar, its legs sweep into diagonal legs, and its antenna pops up as a neat top-right dot, forming the central 犬 component.

[00:04.5 - 00:08.0] Assembly & 3.5-Second Hold:
The strokes lock together seamlessly to complete the precise Traditional Chinese glyph 器. The dark-indigo glyph fills roughly 70% of the frame height, centered against the warm, clean background with clear margins. The glyph stays completely static with no motion or camera drift for the final 3.5 seconds.

Audio:
An off-screen voice speaks clearly in Taiwanese Mandarin: "器、器、機器人" (qì, qì, jī qì rén), timed naturally with the finished glyph display. There are no subtitles, on-screen vocabulary text, or distracting background music.
direction: 用機器人的例子，生動搞笑

conceptZh: 「器」變成一件奇妙樂器：海盜吹氣卻吹翹自己的鬍子，改用輕敲才奏出聲音。
object: A rigid, indigo musical instrument shaped exactly like 器, with its four square openings preserved.
morph: Begin with the complete glyph. Its four square openings function as air ports; all strokes remain rigid and correctly formed throughout.
creativeAngle: 改用完整字形演示「樂器」，避免角色變形造成筆畫混淆。固執鸚鵡拒絕吹奏，逞強海盜反被回流的氣吹翹鬍子；最後輕敲成功，讓笑點與器具的使用直接相連。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D animation with a locked frontal camera and a warm pale-apricot background. Center one solid saturated-indigo Traditional Chinese glyph 器, occupying about 70% of frame height with generous margins. Use a verified Traditional Chinese typeface outline as the exact geometry of a shallow sculptural musical instrument: four crisp square openings and every connecting stroke and small dot remain clearly separated and correctly formed. Keep the complete glyph centered, uncropped and rigid throughout.

An original barrel-shaped wooden toy pirate stands in the left margin, with articulated toy joints, a painted waistcoat, an extravagant curled moustache and an overly confident grin. His sole companion is a small stylized toy parrot on his shoulder. At 0.0–1.6 seconds, the pirate proudly gestures for the parrot to blow into the instrument's lower-left square opening. The parrot folds its wings and pointedly turns its beak away. The pirate pauses, then puffs out his cheeks: he will do it himself.

At 1.6–3.4 seconds, he leans toward the opening without covering its outline and blows. The air travels through the imaginary instrument and immediately escapes from the upper-left opening toward his face. A brief, soft breath puff flips both ends of his moustache straight upward. Hold his wide-eyed double-take for a beat while the parrot remains stubbornly unimpressed. Keep this gentle and quiet; the glyph itself never bends, inflates or sprouts features.

At 3.4–4.6 seconds, the pirate thoughtfully taps the instrument's outside edge with one wooden finger. One soft, pleasing musical tone sounds. His moustache settles, his proud grin returns, and he sidesteps out of frame with the parrot. From 4.6–8.0 seconds, hold the finished glyph completely still and alone for 3.4 seconds, with uniform indigo strokes, clean open counters and no camera movement.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly “器、器、樂器”. Pronounce the first 器 at approximately 0.35 seconds, the second at 1.1 seconds after a short pause, and 樂器 at 5.4–6.4 seconds during the unobstructed final hold. Use qì for 器 and yuè qì for 樂器. No other speech or background music. Keep the breath puff and musical tap softer than the narration. The vocabulary is audio only; the single glyph 器 is the only on-screen text. Use only the invented animated cast and glyph instrument, with no additional props, subtitles, logos, watermarks, floating musical symbols, clutter or flashing effects.
